groups.name: bulk RNA-seq raw count matrix
groups.reason: The two members of set-1 are different substrates consumed by entirely different downstream steps: counts.csv is the numeric expression matrix (the measurement itself), metadata.csv is the sample-to-condition design table used to build a model contrast. A downstream step never treats them interchangeably, so they are split into separate groups despite sharing one filename template.
groups.description: A single gene (rows) x sample (columns) raw integer count matrix: 12,000 genes by 12 samples (sample_01-sample_12), verified to contain only integer values (no decimals), i.e. unnormalized raw counts straight from a quantification pipeline. This is the primary measurement input for differential expression.
groups.memberRepresents: the full gene x sample raw read-count matrix for the experiment (one matrix, not one file per sample)

groups.name: gene length reference table
groups.description: A 2-column, 12,000-row table (gene, length) giving a length value per gene. Its gene set is a 100%-overlap match (12,000/12,000, verified by direct comparison) with the count matrix's gene set, and it is not produced by this experiment -- it is a consumed annotation used for length-based normalization (e.g. TPM/FPKM/RPKM conversion) or length-bias correction in downstream gene-set enrichment (e.g. goseq).
groups.categoryReason: Not a measurement of any sample -- it is a static per-gene annotation table the analysis would consume for normalization, matching the reference-data category's definition of consumed-not-produced canonical inputs.
groups.memberRepresents: a per-gene length lookup covering the same 12,000-gene set as the count matrix

probes.reason: metadata.csv carries only 'sample' and 'condition' columns; there is no subject/patient/donor identifier distinct from the sample ID, so it is not recorded whether one sample corresponds to one distinct biological subject.
no visit/day/cycle column and no timepoint-like tokens; sample IDs are simple sequential numbers (sample_01..sample_12) with no time information.
no plate/lane/run/date/centre column exists in metadata.csv, and no such tokens appear in the sample or gene files.

caveats: Organism is not stated by any input (no organism/species column, no accession, no README/paper); it is inferred at LOW confidence purely from gene-symbol capitalization convention (100% upper-case across 12,000 symbols, consistent with HGNC/human style). Treat any organism-specific reference choice (genome build, pathway database species) as provisional.

Counts are raw integers (confirmed no decimal values) — not normalized, not log-transformed. Standard library-size normalization (DESeq2/edgeR/limma-voom) is required before any comparison; gene_lengths.csv is available if length-normalized units (TPM/FPKM) or length-bias-aware GSEA (e.g. goseq) are needed.

No subject-level identifier is recorded separately from 'sample' — each of the 12 samples is presumably one biological replicate/subject, but this is not stated, so pairing or repeated-measures structure (if any) cannot be verified.

No batch, run-date, plate, or timepoint metadata exists anywhere in the input, so batch effects cannot be assessed or adjusted for; any observed condition effect could be confounded with unrecorded processing batches.

Group sizes are balanced (6 control / 6 treated), which is a strength for a two-group test, but n=6 per arm is small for bulk RNA-seq differential expression and limits power to detect modest effect sizes.
result.summary: The dataset is a small bulk RNA-seq experiment: a raw integer gene x sample count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 samples, verified integer-only, no decimals), a 12-sample metadata sheet assigning each sample to 'control' (n=6) or 'treated' (n=6), and a gene-length lookup table (12,000 genes, 100% overlap with the count matrix's gene set) suitable for length-based normalization (TPM/FPKM/RPKM) or as a covariate for tools like GOseq that correct for gene-length bias. No README, paper, or other documentation is included, and no organism, tissue, or accession metadata is present anywhere in the input; organism is inferred at low confidence from gene-symbol case convention only (see organism.notes). This is a complete, ready-to-use differential-expression input set for a two-group comparison, but it carries no batch, timepoint, subject, or pairing information beyond the sample ID and condition label — the sample IS the unit of observation, and whether one sample equals one distinct biological subject is not stated.

organism.notes: No organism metadata, accession, or document is present in the input set (only counts.csv, metadata.csv, gene_lengths.csv). All 12,000 gene symbols in counts.csv/gene_lengths.csv are fully upper-case (e.g. ABCA1, ACAA2, AARS1) with zero lower-case characters anywhere, consistent with HGNC (human) nomenclature convention as opposed to MGI/RGD title-case mouse/rat symbols (e.g. Abca1). This is an indirect, content-based inference, not a direct statement, so confidence is kept low.

dimensions.label: Treatment arm (control vs treated)
dimensions.description: The dataset's single designed two-arm comparison: metadata.csv assigns each of the 12 samples to exactly one of two design-assigned groups, 'control' or 'treated', with a balanced 6-vs-6 split. This is the comparison the count matrix and gene-length table exist to support.

dimensions.label: Sample identity

nestsUnder.evidence: metadata.csv rows pair each sample value 1:1 with one condition value

dimensions.description: 12 individual samples (sample_01 through sample_12), each one column of the count matrix and one row of metadata.csv. No subject identifier distinct from sample exists, so sample is the atomic unit of observation here; each sample nests under exactly one treatment arm.

result.experimentalDesign: A two-group bulk RNA-seq case/control design: 12 samples (sample_01–sample_12) split evenly into 6 'control' and 6 'treated' per metadata.csv, with matching columns in the 12,000-gene raw count matrix. No pairing, timepoint, or batch information is recorded, so the design reads as a simple unpaired two-arm comparison with n=6 per arm.
